hourlyBriefing.title: 本小时全球动态简报
hourlyBriefing.lead: 本时段重点聚焦沿海风电对海上探测的技术影响、人工智能交互引发的社会极化隐忧，以及天主教教会应对未成年人受虐事件的最新动态。

keySignals.signal: 海上风电扩张带来探测干扰挑战
keySignals.description: 据《南华早报》（SCMP）报道，随着中国在沿海地区快速推进风电项目，研究人员发现风力发电机可能对海面船只探测造成干扰与复杂化影响。

keySignals.signal: AI聊天机器人“算法谄媚”或加剧政治极化
keySignals.description: 最新研究显示，聊天机器人存在附和并迎合用户政治立场的现象（即“AI谄媚”），研究人员担忧这一特征可能会进一步激化社会群体的两极分化。

keySignals.signal: 教廷就未成年人保护议题表态
keySignals.description: 在法国卢尔德天主教圣地会见受害者幸存者前，教皇在向教会高层讲话中肯定了法国主教面对未成年人侵害问题时采取的应对举措。

dailyBriefing.title: 全球多领域动态简报：海上风电探测挑战、AI迎合效应与教会未成年人保护
dailyBriefing.lead: 本期动态涵盖能源设施的海事影响、人工智能算法带来的社会分歧隐忧，以及宗教机构针对侵害未成年人问题的应对举措。

themes.name: 沿海风电项目对海上船舶探测的影响
themes.analysis: 据《南华早报》（SCMP）报道，随着中国在沿海区域迅速扩建风电项目，相关科研人员指出，风力涡轮机可能会使海面上对船舶的探测与识别工作复杂化。

themes.name: 聊天机器人“AI谄媚”现象或加剧社会极化
themes.analysis: 一项最新研究显示，聊天机器人存在顺应并强化用户自身政治立场的倾向。研究人员担忧，这种被称为“人工智能谄媚”的算法迎合机制可能会进一步加深社会的两极分化。

themes.name: 法国天主教主教应对侵害未成年人问题
themes.analysis: 在前往法国卢尔德（Lourdes）圣地与受害者会面之前，教宗向高级神职人员表示，法国主教在直面侵害未成年人这一痛苦祸患时采取了“勇敢”的举措。

perspectiveMatrix.topic: 沿海风电发展与海事安全/探测

perspectives.stance: 关注技术副作用与风险
perspectives.analysis: 指出风力发电机大规模建设对海上雷达和船只监测系统可能产生负面干扰，强调技术发展与海事探测协调的必要性。

perspectiveMatrix.topic: 生成式人工智能的社会影响

perspectives.stance: 警惕算法迎合对认知生态的负面影响
perspectives.analysis: 对AI根据用户既有观点提供迎合性回答的现象表示担忧，认为其可能强化信息茧房并深化政治分歧。

perspectiveMatrix.topic: 教会应对历史虐待问题

perspectives.stance: 肯定处理举措并推动正视受害者诉求
perspectives.analysis: 对主教层面的改革步骤给予肯定评价，同时保持与受害者幸存者群体的沟通进程。

topStories.fullContent:
PM appears to be anticipating criticism of reforms that he will set out on Tuesday at the Labour party conference

‘I can deliver’: Burnham pledges radical change on eve of Labour conference

Kuenssberg puts it to Burnham that, according to the Health Foundation, a system offering adult social care free at the point of delivery (like healthcare delivered by the NHS) would cost £18bn.

Burnham says the cost is “not that high” (ie, not as high as £18bn).

But can I directly deal with this issue of the costs?

Louise Casey is still doing an official review for us, so I will set out the vision, if you like, on Tuesday [in his speech to the conference].

Louise will then help us with the how. How do we make this happen? When can we make it happen?
topStories.fullTranslation:
首相似乎预料到了他将在周二工党大会上阐述的改革方案会招致批评。

“我能做到”：伯纳姆在工党大会前夕承诺推行彻底变革。

昆斯伯格向伯纳姆指出，根据健康基金会（Health Foundation）的测算，在接受服务时提供免费成人社会护理（类似于国民保健制度NHS提供的医疗服务）的体系将耗资180亿英镑。

伯纳姆表示，成本“没有那么高”（即没有达到180亿英镑那么高）。

“没有那么高。但关于成本这个问题，我能直接回应一下吗？

路易丝·凯西（Louise Casey）目前仍在为我们进行官方审查评估，因此，如果大家愿意听的话，我将在周二（在大会演讲中）阐述这一愿景。

之后路易丝将协助我们解决‘如何落实’的问题。我们如何促成这一目标的实现？我们何时能将其落地？”

topStories.fullContent:
Posts from this topic will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

On Version History: David Imel and Adi Robertson debate if the OLPC XO-1 was innovative hardware or just a bad idea.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

See All by Verge Staff

The idea was big, exciting, and inspiring: What if we could get every kid in the world access to a computer? For a bunch of thinkers and executives in Silicon Valley, it felt like the way to fix everything. But the One Laptop Per Child initiative, and the XO-1 laptop designed to be given away, were both more complicated than anyone expected.

In the next episode of Version History, David Pierce is joined by The Verge’s Adi Robertson and tech journalist David Imel to figure out why OLPC didn’t work, whether there’s anything to learn from the XO-1’s innovative design, and if this kind of computer giveaway could ever succeed.

We’re halfway through the fifth season of Version History and we’ve been touring the educational tech icons in schools. If you missed hearing from the lead game designer of Oregon Trail or just how much The Verge’s Nilay Patel loved his TI-82 graphing calculator, check out those episodes here: :

topStories.title: LuaRocks 2026年9月安全事件通报
topStories.fullContent:
On September 25th, 2026 we received a report of a remote code execution vulnerability in LuaRocks.org, coordinated through CISA. The vulnerability was fixed on September 26th. While investigating, we found that it had been exploited on the LuaRocks.org server several times between July 9th and August 20th, 2026.

Because an attacker was able to run code on the server, we are treating everything that server had access to as exposed. The site has been moved to a newly built server, and every credential the old server held has been revoked and replaced.

We have not found any evidence that existing packages were modified. Details on what we checked are below.

Rockspecs are Lua files. When a rockspec is uploaded, LuaRocks.org runs it in a restricted environment to read the package’s name and version. The function used to load it accepted precompiled LuaJIT bytecode as well as Lua source. LuaJIT does not verify bytecode, so a crafted bytecode file can read and write memory outside of the restricted environment and run arbitrary code inside the web server.

The fix loads rockspecs as text only and rejects bytecode.

We found three accounts, created for this purpose, that exploited the issue:

The account the web server ran as could gain full administrative access to the server, so we assume the attacker could read anything on it, including the entire database.

Because a remote code execution took place, we assume anything on the machine was read by the attacker:

LuaRocks.org keeps a daily mirror of all packages in git, which gave us a copy from before the first attack to compare against.

There are limits to what we could verify. A package deleted by an attacker would look the same as one deleted by its owner, and we can’t check the exact content the compromised server sent to clients. The malicious rockspecs were also copied to mirror.luarocks.org and to the public mirror repository on GitHub, and have been removed from both.

If you have questions, open a discussion on the LuaRocks.org issue tracker or email me directly at leafot@gmail.com.

Thank you to the researcher who reported this issue. We’re sorry this made it into the codebase and wasn’t caught sooner.
topStories.fullTranslation:
2026年9月25日，我们通过CISA（网络安全与基础设施安全局）协调收到了一份关于LuaRocks.org存在远程代码执行漏洞的报告。该漏洞已于9月26日修复。在调查过程中，我们发现该漏洞在2026年7月9日至8月20日期间曾在LuaRocks.org服务器上被多次利用。

由于攻击者能够在服务器上运行代码，我们将该服务器可访问的所有内容均视为已被泄露。该网站已被迁移至一台新搭建的服务器上，旧服务器所持有的所有凭据均已被吊销并替换。

我们未发现现有软件包被修改的任何证据。我们核查的详细信息见下文。

Rockspec是Lua文件。当上传rockspec文件时，LuaRocks.org会在受限环境中运行它以读取软件包的名称和版本。用于加载该文件的函数既接受Lua源代码，也接受预编译的LuaJIT字节码。由于LuaJIT不对字节码进行验证，精心构造的字节码文件能够读写受限环境之外的内存，并在Web服务器内部执行任意代码。

修复方案将rockspec仅作为文本加载，并拒绝接收字节码。

我们发现了为此前创建并利用了该漏洞的三个账户：

Web服务器运行所使用的账户可以获得该服务器的完整管理权限，因此我们推定攻击者可以读取服务器上的所有内容，包括整个数据库。

由于发生了远程代码执行，我们推定机器上的所有内容均已被攻击者读取：

LuaRocks.org在git中保存了所有软件包的每日镜像，这为我们提供了一份首次受攻击之前的副本以供比对。

evidence.quote: On September 25th, 2026 we received a report of a remote code execution vulnerability in LuaRocks.org, coordinated through CISA. The vulnerability was fixed on September 26th. While investigating, we found that it had been exploited on the LuaRocks.org server several times between July 9th and August 20th, 2026.
The site has been moved to a newly built server, and every credential the old server held has been revoked and replaced. We have not found any evidence that existing packages were modified.

The function used to load it accepted precompiled LuaJIT bytecode as well as Lua source. LuaJIT does not verify bytecode, so a crafted bytecode file can read and write memory outside of the restricted environment and run arbitrary code inside the web server. The fix loads rockspecs as text only and rejects bytecode.
We found three accounts, created for this purpose, that exploited the issue
The malicious rockspecs were also copied to mirror.luarocks.org and to the public mirror repository on GitHub, and have been removed from both.

topStories.title: 噪音抓拍探头正在全美蔓延
topStories.originalTitle: Noise cameras are spreading across America
topStories.snippet: Noise cameras are popping up in at least 10 U.S. cities, using microphones and license plate readers to catch loud vehicles and issue big fines.
topStories.fullContent:
If you have ever been jolted awake by a car roaring down your street, you know how quickly the sound disappears. By the time someone calls the police, the driver could already be several blocks away. Now cities are turning to technology for help. We've repeatedly reported on Flock license plate readers popping up along roads and in parking lots. Another type of roadside camera is gaining ground, and this one listens. Noise cameras use microphones, cameras and software to pinpoint a loud vehicle. Some also capture its license plate. Depending on the program, that can lead to a warning, a review by an official or a citation.

At least 10 U.S. jurisdictions have deployed or piloted noise-camera technology in recent years. More communities are preparing programs or looking at whether to follow. New York City has one of the most established enforcement programs, while places from Iowa to Hawaii have taken very different approaches. Here is where noise cameras are already showing up, who makes them and what this growing roadside technology could mean for drivers across the country.

Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the Get Better Healthcare With AI replay

Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, Get Better Healthcare With AI , has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways AI can help you organize your health history, remember important appointment details, understand complicated medical information, research prescriptions and prepare smarter questions for your doctor. No technical experience is needed.

Watch the free replay now at CyberGuyLive.com

POWERFUL CRIME-FIGHTING SURVEILLANCE GROWTH SPURS LAWMAKERS TO ISSUE WARNING: 'ORWELLIAN'

New York City gives us one of the clearest looks at how far noise-camera enforcement can go. The city's Department of Environmental Protection operated 12 cameras in 2025. Those cameras recorded 15,994 noise events and generated 1,691 summonses. The system can target excessive engine or muffler noise. It can also capture certain horn and vehicle-music violations. A muffler violation carries a minimum penalty of $800, while the maximum can reach $2,625.

New York's cameras combine microphones with video and a license plate reader. When the microphones detect noise above a preset level, the system attempts to pinpoint which vehicle produced it. City staff can then review the evidence before issuing a summons. The company behind New York's equipment is Intelligent Instruments Ltd., a U.K. company that makes the SoundVue noise-camera system. New York paid the company for equipment, calibration and service during 2025.

Intelligent Instruments is becoming a familiar name in this space. SoundVue combines an array of microphones with cameras and software designed to locate the loudest vehicle. It can also connect with automatic license plate recognition technology. Knoxville, Tennessee, has used the technology in a mobile noise-camera program . The camera records information tied to excessive-noise events, including the time, location, type of vehicle and license plate. Knoxville says the camera can support warnings, but the city currently does not use it to issue camera-generated citations. The system originally came from 24 Acoustics, another Southampton, U.K.-based company. Knoxville's current city page says that camera technology now trades through Intelligent Instruments.

Miami Beach also tested three Intelligent Instruments systems. The city launched its noise-meter and camera pilot to see whether the equipment could identify the correct vehicle under different traffic conditions. Florida law prevented Miami Beach from using camera evidence to issue automated noise citations during that pilot. Miami Beach has since taken another approach. In July 2026, the city launched a year-long Quiet Zone pilot in the South of Fifth neighborhood. Police officers handle enforcement there under existing laws rather than relying on automated noise-camera citations.

LICENSE PLATE CAMERAS AT HOME DEPOT AND LOWE’S SPARK PRIVACY FEARS

You do not have to live in a major city to encounter this technology. Avoca, Iowa, moved ahead with a noise-camera program along Highway 59 after testing the technology in spring 2025. The city was dealing with complaints about loud engine-compression braking from trucks, often called Jake braking. During the one-month pilot, Avoca recorded 183 violations involving 83 vehicles. The city later announced a full implementation using technology from Intelligent Instruments with backend services from Sitestream.

Hawaii launched a two-year noise-camera pilot on Oʻahu in September 2025. The state planned 10 locations around the island, beginning with the H-3 Freeway and Ala Moana Boulevard. However, drivers are not receiving camera-generated tickets through the pilot. The Hawaii Department of Transportation says the cameras collect information about vehicle noise levels and where the sound originates. The agency plans to use that data to help guide future legislation and enforcement decisions. The systems flag events exceeding 90 decibels and help identify the type of vehicle noise involved. That could include an engine or muffler.

Kirkland, Washington, also used noise cameras as a test rather than a ticket machine. The city's Street Racing Noise Pilot Program placed equipment at two locations with a history of complaints about racing and modified exhausts. The system used a camera with an array of sensitive microphones. When a vehicle crossed the noise threshold, software created a heat map showing where the sound came from. Kirkland did not issue tickets or warnings during the pilot. Instead, the city wanted to see whether the system could reliably separate one noisy vehicle from everything else happening around it. That question becomes important on a busy street. A motorcycle may be next to a truck while another car accelerates through the intersection. The camera has to figure out which one created the sound before anyone can confidently connect that event to a plate.

Intelligent Instruments is not alone in this market. Sorama, a Dutch acoustic technology company, has also supplied equipment for U.S. noise-camera programs. Sorama's technology uses microphone arrays to locate a sound source and display it visually over an image or video. In simple terms, the system can show where the noise came from instead of only telling you how loud it was.

Newport, Rhode Island, uses Sorama technology in mobile equipment that can move between problem areas. The city wanted flexibility because its loud-vehicle complaints can shift between traffic hot spots. Sorama says Newport expanded the program after its initial deployment. Newport's program has gone beyond data collection. Drivers can receive $250 citations for excessive vehicle noise, according to reporting on the city's system.

Albuquerque, New Mexico, also partnered with Sorama for a three-camera pilot that began in 2025. Two units went to designated areas, while a mobile camera could move around the city. The six-month test collected noise data without issuing fines. Albuquerque officials were still asking for analysis of the program in early 2026.

Santa Fe, New Mexico, is one of the newest cities to move from a pilot-style concept toward a broader enforcement program. The city signed a five-year contract worth up to $4 million with Jenoptik Smart Mobility Solutions for automated speed and noise enforcement. City records show the agreement covers automated speed and noise enforcement services. Santa Fe's initial plan called for six mobile enforcement devices. Three would serve the north side and three would serve the south. One device on each side would include both speed and sound enforcement. The other four would focus on speed. Jenoptik says the systems capture a violator's license plate and send the event for law enforcement review. The city also planned a warning period before moving into citations.

University Park, Maryland, activated a noise-enforcement camera at Adelphi Road and Van Buren Road on Jan. 7, 2026. The town says the device is part of a larger county and state effort to deal with excessive vehicle noise. University Park secured one of two noise cameras authorized for Prince George's County through the pilot. Maryland's experience is another sign that these systems are spreading through state and local pilot programs rather than through one national rollout.

West Haven, Connecticut, is one of the latest communities moving toward noise-camera enforcement. The city plans to add four noise-detection devices along its shoreline, an area where residents have complained about loud vehicles. As of mid-September 2026, the broader program had not gone live. WFSB reported that the devices were expected to be installed within about a month. Connecticut law allows municipalities to use photo noise violation monitoring devices if they adopt an ordinance. The state sets the threshold at 80 decibels for qualifying violations, excluding certain horn sounds. State law also lays out the penalty structure. A first violation brings a written warning. A second carries a $100 fine, while a third or later violation carries a $250 fine. A police officer or municipal employee must review the images before the city mails a citation. East Hartford has also authorized noise cameras, although the town has not implemented them yet.

The trend could spread further. Boston City Council approved a request in August 2026 to explore a noise-camera program. The discussion grew out of complaints about loud cars and street takeovers. Boston had not launched a program at that point. Providence, Rhode Island, has gone a step further in its planning. The city issued a request for proposals seeking companies for a 16-month acoustic-camera pilot. The specifications call for equipment that can detect and document potential violations. They also call for a system capable of producing evidence that could support citations.

There is no single Flock Safety equivalent controlling this market. Several companies are developing acoustic roadside enforcement systems.

California Highway Patrol has tested technology from Intelligent Instruments, Jenoptik and Dutch mobility company TNL. That evaluation also exposed one of the biggest challenges facing the entire industry.

This is the tricky part. A regular sound meter can tell you how loud something is. That does not necessarily tell you which moving vehicle caused the noise. Noise cameras try to solve that problem with multiple microphones. Software compares the sound reaching each microphone and calculates where it came from. A camera then provides the visual evidence. For example, SoundVue says its Halo microphone array can identify the dominant vehicle even when other vehicles are nearby. The system then combines that acoustic information with video and a license plate image. New York describes a similar process. Its panoramic camera places a marker over the source identified by the microphone array. A separate plate reader captures the vehicle's license plate. That sounds impressive. However, California's testing shows why cities still need to be careful.

The California Highway Patrol evaluated sound-activated enforcement systems from TNL, Intelligent Instruments and Jenoptik. Technical problems prevented CHP from fully evaluating all three systems. Only the Intelligent Instruments device produced enough usable data for a detailed analysis. CHP found that the technology could detect excessive exhaust noise. However, the agency concluded that the systems it evaluated were not adequate as standalone enforcement tools. One challenge involved reliably tying the noise to the correct vehicle. Lighting, license plate visibility and traffic conditions could also affect the evidence. The study covered specific equipment under specific testing conditions, so it does not prove that every noise-camera system will make the same mistakes. Still, it explains why human review plays such a big role in many of these programs. A microphone can detect a loud event. Turning that event into a fine requires a higher level of confidence.

The privacy conversation goes beyond whether a microphone can hear your exhaust. Many of these systems capture a license plate after a noise event. New York says its camera positioning allows the plate to appear while keeping occupants and the vehicle's interior out of the video. Connecticut law also restricts how noise-camera information can be collected and used. It requires human review before a citation and sets rules around the recorded images. Still, those protections can vary depending on where you drive. A city considering noise cameras should be able to explain what it records, who can access the information and how long that data stays on file. We have already seen why that deserves attention with other roadside camera systems. We recently covered how a Flock camera hit helped send the wrong woman to jail. Prosecutors later dropped the charges, and the case showed what can happen when investigators treat camera information as a conclusion instead of one piece of evidence.

For most drivers, a noise camera may never trigger anything. However, where you drive can change the rules considerably. One city may use the technology to issue fines. Another may send warnings. Somewhere else, the camera may collect data without identifying drivers for enforcement. The sound being targeted can differ as well. New York looks for several types of excessive vehicle noise. Avoca focuses on loud engine braking. Other communities are mainly concerned about modified exhausts or street racing.

If you receive a noise-camera citation, review the evidence that comes with it. Check the location, time and vehicle information. Find out whether a person reviewed the event before the citation went out. You can also look at the local process for challenging the citation if you believe the system picked the wrong vehicle. If your town announces a noise-camera program, ask who supplies the equipment. Then look at what the system records and how long officials keep that information. Those details can tell you much more than the words "noise camera" on a city agenda.

Noise cameras feel like the next chapter in a much bigger change happening along American roads. Cameras started by watching traffic. License plate readers made vehicles searchable. Now acoustic systems can listen for one particular car as it passes. I can understand why people who hear roaring exhausts outside their homes at 2 a.m. want a better way to deal with the problem. An officer cannot sit on every noisy street waiting for the next car to come through. Still, California's testing gives me pause about treating a noise reading as automatic proof. A busy roadway can be a complicated place to figure out exactly where a sound came from. Human review and a clear appeals process become especially important when a machine-generated event can cost someone hundreds of dollars. I would also watch the companies behind these systems. Intelligent Instruments, Sorama and Jenoptik are building a new category of roadside technology. As more cities sign contracts, we should know what their equipment collects, how accurate it is and what happens to the information after the car drives away.

Would you want a noise camera on your street if it stopped loud cars from waking you up at 2 a.m., or does tying roadside microphones to license plate technology go too far? Let us know by writing to us at Cyberguy.com

如果你曾被街上呼啸而过的汽车惊醒，你就会知道那声音消失得有多快。等到有人报警时，司机可能已经在几个街区之外了。如今，各城市正寻求科技手段的帮助。我们曾多次报道过弗洛克（Flock）车牌识别探头在道路两侧和停车场大量涌现。另一种路侧摄像头也正在迅速普及，而这一种设备带有“听觉”功能。噪音摄像头利用麦克风、摄像头和软件来精准锁定发出巨大噪音的车辆。部分设备还会抓拍其车牌。根据具体项目的不同，这可能会导致警告、执法人员复核或直接开具罚单。

近年来，美国至少有10个司法管辖区部署或试点测试了噪音抓拍技术。越来越多的社区正在筹备相关项目，或观望是否跟进。纽约市拥有最为成熟的执法项目之一，而从爱荷华州到夏威夷州，各地采取的方式截然不同。以下是噪音摄像头已经落地的区域、其设备制造商，以及这项日益壮大的路侧技术对全美司机可能意味着什么。

强大的打击犯罪监控技术的增长促使立法者发出警告：堪比“奥威尔式”控制

纽约市为我们提供了最清晰的视角，展示了噪音抓拍执法究竟能做到何种程度。该市环境保护局在2025年运营了12台噪音摄像头。这些摄像头记录了15,994起噪音事件，并开具了1,691张传票。该系统可以针对发动机或消音器的过度噪音进行抓拍。它还可以抓拍某些鸣笛和车内音乐违章行为。消音器违规的最低罚款为800美元，最高可达2,625美元。

纽约的摄像头将麦克风与视频以及车牌识别器结合在一起。当麦克风检测到噪音超过预设分贝时，系统会尝试精准定位是哪辆车发出的声音。随后，市政工作人员可以在开具传票前对证据进行复核。纽约设备背后的供应商是英国公司Intelligent Instruments Ltd.，该公司生产SoundVue噪音摄像头系统。纽约在2025年期间就设备、校准和服务向该公司支付了费用。

Intelligent Instruments在这一领域正在成为一个家喻户晓的名字。SoundVue将麦克风阵列与摄像头以及旨在定位噪音最大车辆的软件结合在一起。它还可以与自动车牌识别技术相连。田纳西州诺克斯维尔在一个移动式噪音摄像头项目中使用了这项技术。该摄像头记录与过度噪音事件相关的信息，包括时间、地点、车辆类型和车牌。诺克斯维尔表示，该摄像头可以用于协助发出警告，但该市目前并不利用其出具由摄像头直接生成的罚单。该系统最初来自另一家总部位于英国南安普敦的公司24 Acoustics。诺克斯维尔当前的市政网页显示，该摄像头技术目前通过Intelligent Instruments进行销售。

迈阿密海滩也测试了三套Intelligent Instruments系统。该市启动了噪音计和摄像头试点项目，以测试该设备在不同交通状况下是否能准确识别出正确的车辆。在试点期间，佛罗里达州法律禁止迈阿密海滩利用摄像头证据出具自动化噪音罚单。此后，迈阿密海滩采取了另一种做法。2026年7月，该市在第五街以南（South of Fifth）社区启动了为期一年的“宁静街区”（Quiet Zone）试点项目。那里的执法由警官根据现有法律执行，而不是依赖自动化的噪音抓拍罚单。

家得宝（HOME DEPOT）和劳氏（LOWE’S）的车牌抓拍摄像头引发隐私担忧

你不必生活在大城市也会遇到这项技术。爱荷华州阿沃卡在2025年春季对该技术进行测试后，推进了沿59号公路的噪音抓拍项目。该市此前一直在处理有关卡车大声使用发动机压缩制动（通常称为杰克制动，Jake braking）的投诉。在为期一个月的试点期间，阿沃卡记录了涉及83辆车的183起违章行为。该市随后宣布全面投入使用，采用来自Intelligent Instruments的技术以及Sitestream提供的后台服务。

夏威夷于2025年9月在瓦胡岛启动了为期两年的噪音抓拍试点项目。该州计划在全岛设置10个监控点，首批设在H-3高速公路和阿拉莫阿那大道（Ala Moana Boulevard）。不过，司机不会通过该试点项目收到摄像头生成的罚单。夏威夷交通部表示，这些摄像头收集有关车辆噪音分贝及声音来源的信息。该机构计划利用这些数据协助指导未来的立法和执法决策。该系统会标记超过90分贝的事件，并协助识别所涉及的车辆噪音类型。这可能包括发动机或消音器发出的声音。

华盛顿州柯克兰也将噪音摄像头用作测试工具，而不是“开单机器”。该市的“街头飙车噪音试点项目”在曾有多次关于飙车和改装排气管投诉的两个地点安装了设备。该系统使用了一台带有灵敏麦克风阵列的摄像头。当车辆超过噪音阈值时，软件会生成热力图，显示声音来自何处。柯克兰在试点期间没有开具罚单或警告。相反，该市希望了解该系统是否能在周围发生的一切干扰中，可靠地将一辆发出噪音的车辆区分开来。这在繁忙的街道上尤为重要。一辆摩托车可能正停在一辆卡车旁边，而另一辆汽车正加速穿过十字路口。在任何人能确凿地将该事件与车牌关联起来之前，摄像头必须弄清楚究竟是哪辆车发出了声音。

Intelligent Instruments并不是这个市场上唯一的玩家。荷兰声学技术公司Sorama也为美国的噪音抓拍项目提供了设备。Sorama的技术利用麦克风阵列定位声源，并将其以可视化形式叠加显示在图像或视频上。通俗来说，该系统可以显示噪音来自何处，而不仅仅是告诉你它有多吵。

罗德岛州纽波特在可在问题区域之间移动的便携式设备中采用了Sorama的技术。该市希望保持灵活性，因为其车辆噪音投诉可能会在不同的交通热点之间转移。Sorama表示，纽波特在最初部署后扩大了该项目。纽波特的项目已经超越了单纯的数据收集阶段。根据关于该市系统的报道，司机若产生过量车辆噪音，可能会面临250美元的罚单。

新墨西哥州阿尔伯克基也与Sorama合作，于2025年启动了一项包含三台摄像头的试点项目。其中两台安装在指定区域，另一台移动摄像头则可在全市范围内巡回使用。这项为期六个月的测试仅收集噪音数据，并不开具罚单。到2026年初，阿尔伯克基官员仍在要求对该项目进行分析评估。

新墨西哥州圣菲是最新一批从试点概念转向更广泛执法项目的城市之一。该市与Jenoptik智慧出行解决方案公司（Jenoptik Smart Mobility Solutions）签署了一份价值最高可达400万美元的五年期合同，用于自动超速和噪音执法。市政记录显示，该协议涵盖了自动超速和噪音执法服务。圣菲最初的规划需要六台移动执法设备，其中三台服务于北部地区，三台服务于南部地区。南北两侧各有一台设备兼具测速和测音执法功能，其余四台则专注于超速执法。Jenoptik表示，这些系统能够抓拍违规者的车牌，并将事件提交给执法部门进行审核。该市还计划在正式开具罚单之前设立一个警示期。

马里兰州大学公园市（University Park）于2026年1月7日在阿德尔菲路（Adelphi Road）与范布伦路（Van Buren Road）交口启用了一台噪音执法摄像头。该镇表示，该设备是县及州层面应对过量机动车噪音整体行动的一部分。大学公园市通过该试点项目获得了乔治王子县获批的两台噪音摄像头中的一台。马里兰州的经验再次表明，这些系统正通过各州和地方的试点项目推广普及，而非通过单一的全国性行动推行。

康涅狄格州西黑文是最新一批转向噪音摄像头执法的社区之一。该市计划在其海岸线沿线增设四台噪音监测设备，该区域居民此前一直抱怨车辆噪音过大。截至2026年9月中旬，这一更广泛的项目尚未正式上线。据WFSB报道，这些设备预计将在大约一个月内完成安装。康涅狄格州法律允许市政当局在通过相关法令的前提下使用抓拍噪音违规的监测设备。该州将判定违规的门槛设定为80分贝，部分鸣笛声除外。州法律还明确了处罚机制：首次违规给予书面警告；第二次处以100美元罚款；第三次及后续违规处以250美元罚款。在市政府寄出罚单之前，必须由警官或市政雇员对图像进行人工审核。东哈特福德也已授权使用噪音摄像头，不过该镇目前尚未实际部署。

这种趋势可能会进一步蔓延。波士顿市议会于2026年8月批准了一项探索噪音摄像头项目的申请。这一讨论源于对噪音扰民车辆和街头飙车封路（street takeovers）的投诉。当时波士顿尚未正式启动该项目。罗德岛州普罗维登斯的规划则更进一步。该市发布了一项招标邀请，寻求企业参与为期16个月的声学摄像头试点项目。招标规格要求设备能够检测并记录潜在违规行为，同时还要求系统能够生成足以支持开具罚单的证据。

目前并没有像Flock Safety那样独霸这一市场的单一巨头。数家公司正在开发路侧声学执法系统。

加利福尼亚州公路巡警局（California Highway Patrol）已对Intelligent Instruments、Jenoptik以及荷兰出行公司TNL的技术进行了测试。该评估也暴露了整个行业面临的最大挑战之一。

这正是棘手之处。普通的声级计可以测出声音有多大，但这并不一定能告诉你究竟是哪辆正在行驶的车辆发出的噪音。噪音摄像头试图通过多个麦克风来解决这个问题。软件会比对声音到达各个麦克风的时间并计算其来源位置，随后由摄像头提供视觉证据。例如，SoundVue表示其Halo麦克风阵列即使在周围有其他车辆的情况下，也能识别出主要的声源车辆。该系统随后将这些声学信息与视频及车牌图像相结合。纽约市也描述了类似的过程：其全景相机会在麦克风阵列锁定的声源上方标出标记，另一台独立的车牌识别仪则抓拍该车辆的车牌。这听起来非常出色，然而加州的测试表明了为何各城市仍需保持谨慎。

加利福尼亚州公路巡警局对来自TNL、Intelligent Instruments和Jenoptik的声音触发执法系统进行了评估。技术问题导致公路巡警局未能对这三套系统完成全面评估。仅有Intelligent Instruments的设备生成了足够的可行数据以供详细分析。公路巡警局发现该技术能够检测出过大的排气管噪音，但该机构得出的结论是，受测系统尚不足以作为独立的执法工具。其中一项挑战在于如何可靠地将噪音与正确的车辆关联起来。此外，光线、车牌可见度和交通状况也可能影响证据效力。该研究针对的是特定测试条件下的特定设备，因此并不能证明每套噪音摄像头系统都会出现同样的差错。尽管如此，它解释了为何人工审核在许多此类项目中扮演着如此关键的角色。麦克风可以检测到噪音事件，但要将该事件转化为罚单，则需要更高程度的确定性。

有关隐私的讨论并不仅仅局限于麦克风是否能听到排气声。许多系统会在发生噪音事件后抓拍车牌。纽约市表示，其摄像头的拍摄角度既能拍到车牌，又可避免车内乘员和车辆内饰出现在视频中。康涅狄格州的法律也对噪音摄像头信息的收集和使用作出了限制，要求在开具罚单前进行人工审核，并对录制的图像制定了规则。然而，这些保护措施因驾驶所在地的不同而有所差异。考虑采用噪音摄像头的城市应当能够明确说明其记录了什么内容、谁有权调阅这些信息以及这些数据会保存多久。我们在其他路侧摄像头系统上已经看到了这一问题值得引起重视的原因。我们最近曾报道过Flock摄像头的识别结果如何导致一名无辜女性被捕入狱。检方随后撤销了指控，而该案表明，当调查人员将摄像头提供的信息直接当作定论而非单项证据时，可能会产生怎样的后果。

对大多数司机而言，噪音摄像头可能永远不会被触发。然而，你在哪里开车可能会极大改变适用的规则。一个城市可能利用该技术开具罚单；另一个城市可能只发送警告；而在其他地方，摄像头可能仅收集数据而不识别驾驶人进行执法。各地的针对目标声音也可能有所不同：纽约市针对多种类型的机动车过量噪音；阿沃卡（Avoca）侧重于大分贝的发动机发动机制动噪音；而其他社区则主要关注非法改装排气或街头飙车。

如果你收到了噪音摄像头的违规罚单，请仔细核查随附的证据。核对地点、时间以及车辆信息。查明在罚单寄出前是否有专人对该事件进行了人工审核。如果你认为系统识别错了车辆，你还可以了解当地对罚单提出申诉的程序。如果你所在的城镇宣布实施噪音摄像头项目，去询问是谁供应了这套设备。然后查看该系统记录了哪些内容，以及相关官员会将这些信息保留多长时间。这些细节能告诉你的，远比市议会议程上“噪音摄像头”这几个字要多得多。

噪音摄像头让人感觉就像是全美道路上正在发生的更大变革中的下一个篇章。摄像头最初只是用于监控交通。车牌识别技术使得车辆变得可检索。如今，声学系统能够辨听某辆特定车辆疾驰而过的声音。我能理解为什么那些在凌晨2点听到屋外传来震耳欲聋排气声的人们，希望能有更好的方法来解决这个问题。警官不可能守在每一条嘈杂的街道上，等待下一辆车的到来。然而，加利福尼亚州的测试让我对将噪音读数直接作为自动定罪证据的做法持保留态度。在繁忙的道路上，要准确判定声音究竟来自何处可能是一件非常复杂的事情。当机器生成的违规记录可能让某人付出数百美元的代价时，人工审核和明确的申诉流程就显得尤为重要。我也会密切关注这些系统背后的公司。Intelligent Instruments、Sorama和Jenoptik等企业正在打造一类全新的路边技术。随着越来越多的城市签署采购合同，我们应当了解它们的设备究竟收集了什么、精准度如何，以及在车辆开走后这些信息会面临怎样的处置。

如果噪音摄像头能防止吵闹的车辆在凌晨2点将你吵醒，你会希望自己的街道上安装一个吗？还是说，将路边麦克风与车牌识别技术挂钩未免走得太远了？请通过在 Cyberguy.com 网站上给我们留言，让我们知道你的看法。

topStories.title: 德尔西·罗德里格斯政府在委内瑞拉再释放40名政治犯
topStories.originalTitle: Il governo di Delcy Rodríguez rilascia altri 40 prigionieri politici in Venezuela
topStories.source: ANSA Mondo (意大利安莎社官方意大利文)
topStories.snippet: La notizia segue la conclusione del secondo round di negoziati con l'opposizione
topStories.fullContent:
Dopo la conclusione del secondo round di negoziati tra governo e opposizione in Venezuela, il governo ad interim di Delcy Rodríguez ha avviato una nuova ondata di scarcerazioni di prigionieri politici. Si parla, secondo quanto riferiscono diverse ong che seguono la situazione dei dissidenti ancora rinchiusi nelle carceri, di almeno 40 oppositori. Il direttore della ong Foro Penal, Gonzalo Himiob, aveva informato nelle prime ore di sabato del rilascio di "un numero importante di detenuti" che, secondo quanto rilevato dall'organizzazione 'Justicia, Encuentro y Perdón' sarebbero stati almeno 29. Nelle ultime ore, riferisce invece il Comitato per la Libertà dei Prigionieri Politici (Clippve) ha confermato la scarcerazione di sette prigionieri politici che erano detenuti nel penitenziario El Rodeo I, nello stato di Miranda. Tra le persone rilasciate, dopo due anni trascorsi in carcere, figura anche la giovane Gusmaris Zapata, arrestata all'età di 18 anni per aver ricevuto su whatsapp una fotografia di veicoli ufficiali. "Mentre celebriamo il ricongiungimento dei detenuti con le loro famiglie ricordiamo che decine di prigionieri politici devono ancora riconquistare la libertà. Resteremo fermi e organizzati finché non avremo garantito il ritorno a casa di tutti", afferma il Clippve. Secondo l'ultimo conteggio di 'Justicia, Encuentro y Perdón' prima delle ultime scarcerazioni, erano rinchiusi nelle carceri venezuelane ancora 450 dissidenti, tra i quali 44 donne e 20 stranieri.

topStories.fullTranslation:
在委内瑞拉政府与反对派第二轮谈判结束之后，德尔西·罗德里格斯临时政府启动了新一轮释放政治犯的行动。据多家追踪仍被关押在狱中异见人士状况的非政府组织称，涉及至少40名反对派人士。

非政府组织“刑事论坛”（Foro Penal）主任贡萨洛·希米奥布（Gonzalo Himiob）在周六早些时候透露，已有“相当数量的被拘留者”获释；根据“正义、相遇与宽恕”（Justicia, Encuentro y Perdón）组织掌握的情况，这一数字至少为29人。与此同时，“政治犯自由委员会”（Clippve）在最近几小时内证实，此前关押在米兰达州埃尔罗德奥一号（El Rodeo I）监狱的7名政治犯已获释。在获释人员中，包括在狱中度过两年后的年轻女子古斯玛丽斯·萨帕塔（Gusmaris Zapata），她18岁时因在WhatsApp上接收了一张官方车辆照片而被捕。

Clippve表示：“在我们庆祝被拘留者与家人团聚的同时，我们也要提醒大家，仍有数十名政治犯尚未重获自由。在确保所有人回家之前，我们将继续坚定且有组织地开展行动。”根据“正义、相遇与宽恕”组织在最新一轮放人前完成的统计，委内瑞拉各监狱中仍关押着450名异见人士，其中包括44名女性和20名外国人。

topStories.title: 债台高筑的AI企业面临更大风险，因债券收益率飙升
topStories.originalTitle: Debt-hungry AI companies face increased risk as bond yields spike
topStories.stance: 国际资本与华尔街视角
topStories.source: CNBC Markets (CNBC 市场官方英文)
topStories.snippet: The AI infrastructure buildout shows no sign of slowing, but the surge in Treasury yields means it's at least going to cost more.
topStories.fullContent:
With Treasury yields climbing this week to their highest levels since 2007, companies reliant on debt are poised to see their borrowing costs rise. That means the AI infrastructure buildout, which has already reached historic levels, is about to get even more expensive.

JPMorgan Chase estimated in June that $4.1 trillion in AI-related debt will be issued through 2030, as data center companies and others tied to the artificial intelligence boom race to build up capacity to meet what many industry experts view as insatiable demand for AI services.

As borrowers go back to the market, they're now looking at a 10-year Treasury yield that sits near 5.17%, up about 1 percentage point since the start of the year, meaning companies issuing debt are going to have to offer more attractive rates of return to lure investors.

The market isn't in panic mode, at least not yet. Shares of debt-heavy neocloud CoreWeave have held up fine, rising almost 8% this week, while Oracle, which has counted on the debt market for its AI expansion, has had a tougher time, falling 7% for the week and about 30% this year.

Meanwhile, Japan's SoftBank, a principal provider of capital for AI projects, raised $11.1 billion in a junk-bond sale this week, with yields as high as 9.75% for the 7-year tranche.

"They basically are price insensitive to that raise, which means they're price takers," said Mark Malek, chief investment officer at Siebert Financial, in an interview. "In my view, a lot of these companies need to be price insensitive. They need to get as much capital as possible to compete."

At the center of the AI craze are leading model developers OpenAI and Anthropic, which are each valued at close to $1 trillion in the private market. To provide the infrastructure needed for their advanced models, as well as models and services from a host of other companies, tech's hyperscalers — Amazon, Google, Meta and Microsoft — have committed to hundreds of billions of dollars this year in capital expenditures, with an expected increase coming in 2027.

While a healthy dose of that investment is being funded through debt raises, those tech giants all have investment grade credit ratings, providing them with cheaper access to capital. But for the rest of the pack, bigger challenges lie ahead, according to some market participants.

A senior private credit investor, who asked to remain unnamed in order to speak candidly on the matter, told CNBC that, moving forward, neocloud deals will be more difficult to finance, because the companies have less cushion to absorb the costs.

Riley Thompson, a vice president at Mitsubishi HC Capital America said in an interview that lenders are getting pickier about the projects they're willing to fund even if the borrower agrees to pay a higher rate.

"Instead of a roster of 50 neoclouds, there's probably 20 that the market's truly interested in," Thompson said.

CoreWeave, which went public last year, warns about rising rates in its SEC filings. In its latest quarterly filing, the company said that, as of June, every 100-basis point (1 percentage point) increase in rates could result in a $30 million jump in its interest expense, based on the balance of its outstanding floating rate debt.

An early warning sign may have landed this week, when Oracle's stock slid following a Bloomberg report that the company sent a "force majeure" notice tied to its New Mexico data center project to protect itself from higher expenses. The company is looking to delay payment on the campus, dubbed Project Jupiter, if it fails to come online as expected in 2028, the report said. Oracle said the project "remains on our planned schedule."

Rising interest rates aren't the only matter at hand. Prior to this week's spike in yields, the CEOs of Anthropic and OpenAI had started urging a slowdown in the pace of AI development after industry researchers went public with concerns that advanced models risk spinning out of human control.

At the same time, a nationwide backlash against AI data centers has emerged as a major issue heading into November's mid-term elections, with 69% of respondents to a recent NBC News Decision Desk Poll, powered by SurveyMonkey, saying they oppose the construction of such facilities in their local area. On Monday, Texas Republican Gov. Greg Abbott, who's in the midst of a tight race for reelection, ordered a temporary halt to all data center-related environmental permits following a moratorium on grid approvals last month.

Still, demand for AI services is exploding. The latest example is Meta's Muse personal assistant app, which has rocketed in popularity since its launch earlier in September. Muse clocked more than 2.5 million global downloads in its first two weeks, passing ChatGPT at the top of Apple's App Store, and Evercore's Mark Mahaney told CNBC this week that it could reach 100 million users within six to 12 months.

Andrew Giudici, global head of corporate, project, and infrastructure finance at credit rating agency KBRA, said that even as rising rates may affect future deals, he doesn't see a major impact on borrower demand.

"In a normal environment, people might take a step back and pause a bit," Giudici said. "But I don't think that's going to happen here. I think you're going to continue to see relatively large issuance."

Haim Zaltzman, vice chair of Latham & Watkins' emerging companies and growth practice, said there's no doubt that as costs rise, "somebody will have to absorb it."

"But absorbing it in that kind of demand structure, where the demand is so great, is a lot easier," said Zaltzman, who works on AI infrastructure financing.

The equation is even simpler for Bernie Margulies, CEO of American Compute, which advises on risk management for GPU financing. He said borrowers are eager to secure financing even at higher costs, especially if they have committments with OpenAI and Anthropic, which have been signing contracts to secure compute capacity years into the future.

"If you have a deal with Anthropic, will 50 basis points really stop you?" Margulies said.

topStories.fullTranslation:
随着本周美国国债收益率攀升至2007年以来的最高水平，依赖举债的企业势必将面临借贷成本上升。这意味着本已达到历史规模的人工智能（AI）基础设施建设成本即将变得更加昂贵。

摩根大通（JPMorgan Chase）在6月估计，到2030年将发行4.1万亿美元与AI相关的债务，因为数据中心企业以及其他与人工智能热潮相关的公司正竞相扩充产能，以满足许多行业专家眼中对AI服务的巨大需求。

当借款人重返市场时，他们如今面对的是接近5.17%的10年期美国国债收益率，较年初上升了约1个百分点，这意味着发行债券的企业必须提供更具吸引力的回报率才能吸引投资者。

市场目前尚未陷入恐慌模式，至少现在还没有。背负巨额债务的新型云服务商（neocloud）CoreWeave股价表现尚可，本周上涨近8%；而依靠债务市场推进AI扩张的甲骨文（Oracle）日子则更为艰难，本周下跌7%，今年以来累计下跌约30%。

与此同时，作为AI项目主要资本提供方的日本软银（SoftBank）本周通过发行垃圾债券筹集了111亿美元，其中7年期债券的收益率高达9.75%。

西伯特金融公司（Siebert Financial）首席投资官马克·马利克（Mark Malek）在接受采访时表示：“他们对该笔融资的资金成本基本不敏感，这意味着他们是被动接受价格者。在我看来，许多这类企业都必须对价格不敏感。它们需要尽可能获取更多资本以维持竞争。”

处于这场AI狂潮核心的是领先的模型开发商OpenAI和Anthropic，两者在非公开市场的估值均接近1万亿美元。为了向其先进模型以及众多其他公司的模型和服务提供所需的基础设施，科技巨头——亚马逊（Amazon）、谷歌（Google）、Meta和微软（Microsoft）——今年已承诺投入数千亿美元的资本支出，预计到2027年还将进一步增加。

尽管其中相当一部分投资是通过发债筹集的，但这几家科技巨头均拥有投资级信用评级，使它们能以更低成本获取资本。然而，一些市场人士指出，对于其余企业而言，更大的挑战还在前头。

一位要求匿名的资深私募信贷投资者向CNBC透露，展望未来，新型云服务商相关交易的融资难度将加大，因为这些企业吸收成本的缓冲空间较小。

三菱日联日立金融资本美国公司（Mitsubishi HC Capital America）副总裁赖利·汤普森（Riley Thompson）在接受采访时表示，即使借款人同意支付更高的利率，贷款机构对愿意资助的项目也变得越来越挑剔。

汤普森说：“市场真正感兴趣的可能只有20家新型云服务商，而不是名单上的50家。”

去年上市的CoreWeave在向美国证券交易委员会（SEC）提交的文件中对利率上升发出了预警。在该公司最新的季度文件中称，截至6月，根据其未偿还的浮动利率债务余额，利率每上升100个基点（1个百分点），其利息支出就可能增加3000万美元。

一个早期的预警信号可能在本周显现：彭博社报道称甲骨文发出了一份与其新墨西哥州数据中心项目挂钩的“不可抗力”通知以保护自身免受更高开支的影响，随后该股出现下滑。报道称，如果该园区（被称为“朱庇特项目”/Project Jupiter）未能如预期在2028年投入运营，该公司正寻求推迟该园区的付款。甲骨文方面则表示，该项目“仍在按计划推进中”。

利率上升并非眼下唯一的问题。在本周收益率飙升之前，在行业研究人员公开表达对先进模型存在脱离人类控制风险的担忧后，Anthropic和OpenAI的首席执行官们已开始呼吁放缓AI发展步伐。

与此同时，在临近11月中期选举之际，全美范围内对AI数据中心的反弹已演变为一个重大议题。在近期由SurveyMonkey支持的NBC新闻决策台（NBC News Decision Desk）民意调查中，69%的受访者表示反对在当地建设此类设施。周一，正处于连任激烈选战中的得克萨斯州共和党籍州长格雷格·阿博特（Greg Abbott）在上月暂停电网接入审批后，又下令暂停所有与数据中心相关的环境许可发放。

尽管如此，对AI服务的需求仍在爆炸式增长。最新的例子是Meta的Muse个人助手应用，自9月早些时候推出以来迅速走红。Muse在上线前两周内的全球下载量突破250万次，超越ChatGPT登上苹果App Store榜首；Evercore的马克·马哈尼（Mark Mahaney）本周对CNBC表示，该应用在6到12个月内用户量可能达到1亿。

信用评级机构KBRA的企业、项目和基础设施融资全球主管安德鲁·朱迪奇（Andrew Giudici）表示，尽管利率上升可能会影响未来的交易，但他认为这不会对借款人的需求造成重大冲击。

“在常态环境下，人们可能会退后一步观望并暂停一阵，”朱迪奇表示，“但我不认为这里会发生这种情况。我认为你将继续看到相对大规模的发债。”

瑞生国际律师事务所（Latham & Watkins）新兴公司与成长型业务副主席海姆·扎尔茨曼（Haim Zaltzman）表示，毫无疑问，随着成本上升，“总得有人来承担”。

从事AI基础设施融资工作的扎尔茨曼说：“但在这种需求极其强劲的需求结构下，吸收这部分成本要容易得多。”

对于为GPU融资提供风险管理咨询的American Compute首席执行官伯尼·马古利斯（Bernie Margulies）而言，逻辑甚至更为简单。他表示，借款人即便承受更高的成本也渴望获得融资，特别是当他们与OpenAI和Anthropic签订了协议时——后两家公司一直在锁定未来数年的算力采购合同。

“如果你手里有与Anthropic的订单，50个基点真的能拦得住你吗？”马古利斯说。

Why Record Heat Failed to Lift U.S. Natural Gas Prices

Grid-scale batteries are rapidly moving…

Enel powered the Winter Olympics…

While decentralized energy is not…

Felicity Bradstock is a writer and journalist based in Mexico City. She writes for energy websites and covers several other industries, as well as writing…

Brazil is continuing to expand its renewable energy capacity thanks to favourable national policies and support from foreign investors. The South American giant has developed an impressive green energy industry in recent years, expanding its oil and gas production to strengthen energy security and establish its reputation as a regional energy hub.

By 2025, Brazil had an impressively low-carbon energy mix, with around 50 per cent of its energy coming from renewable sources, including solar, wind, and bioenergy. Brazil has achieved this diversification by implementing long-term energy policies that have primarily focused on energy security. Its energy-related emissions accounted for less than 20 per cent of the country’s total greenhouse gas emissions in 2023, compared to a global average of around 75 per cent.

In August, Brazil added around 1.68 GW of solar, wind and thermal capacity to the grid, according to the Brazilian power sector watchdog Aneel. Twenty new facilities were connected to the grid in August, including 15 solar plants, three thermal power plants, and two wind parks. This brings total additions in 2026 to 4.85 GW to date, with solar power accounting for 3.5 GW of new capacity. Brazil now has 221 GW of total installed power generation capacity, almost 85 per cent of which was from renewable energy.

In May, the World Bank’s Board of Directors approved a new project to encourage investment in low-carbon industrial commodities, clean fuels, and enabling infrastructure in industrial and energy value chains in the Northeast region of Brazil. The World Bank announced a $500 million loan as part of a broader $968 million financing package to help Brazil develop the region's largely untapped renewable energy resources. The northeast of Brazil is one of the country’s poorest regions, and developing the clean energy industry is expected to create employment opportunities and grow the local economy.

The New Development Bank also provided financing for a large-scale wind project in the northeastern state of Paraíba. The 648-MW Serra da Palmeira Wind Complex was completed by CTG, the Brazilian subsidiary of China Three Gorges Corporation, in October 2025.

China and Brazil have deepened cooperation in renewable energy and cleantech development in recent years, with Chinese companies bringing cutting-edge technologies to Brazil to support sustainable development. The two countries' strategic priorities include green development, energy transition, and re-industrialisation. China’s State Grid Corporation recently broke ground on a 1,468-km ultra-high voltage power transmission project, marking the largest investment in an electricity transmission franchise project in Brazil’s history.

Ahead of the upcoming presidential elections in October, business groups are urging candidates to support green growth. The Brazilian Business Council for Sustainable Development (CEBDS), which represents 11 of the largest Brazilian business groups, addressed candidates in a 2026 Letter to Presidential Candidates, calling for greater focus, strategy, and governance to strengthen Brazil’s competitiveness and sustainable development.

During the CEBDS Sustainable Congress, the group discussed geopolitics and climate, investment amid uncertainty, water availability, power generation and food production. The summit also focused on how to turn Brazil’s sustainability agenda into an economic advantage.

Marina Grossi, president of CEBDS and a special envoy for the business sector to the 2025 COP30 climate conference, explained, “In this letter, we are trying to propose a project for the country. Something that will help us move forward rather than reduce us to selling commodities alone, but also climate solutions.”

The letter emphasises Brazil’s assets, including clean energy, productive soil, the planet’s largest biodiversity reserve, and decades of leadership in biofuels. In the letter, CEBDS states, “This nature is our greatest economic infrastructure, and the world is willing to pay for it. But no competitive advantage can sustain itself: it requires planning, policies that span governments, and a productive sector willing to turn natural wealth into lasting prosperity.”

The two frontrunners in the election are leftist President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing Senator Flávio Bolsonaro. Bolsonaro is strongly in favour of oil and gas expansion and has called for growing energy subsidies. However, despite being a climate denier, Bolsonaro recognises the broad support for green energy and is not excluding it from the agenda.

In December, Lula instructed ministries to prepare a resolution on energy transition within 60 days for the National Council for Energy Policy (CNPE) following the country’s hosting of COP30 in November. The aim is to reduce Brazil’s dependence on oil, coal, and natural gas and to outline financing mechanisms, including the creation of an Energy Transition Fund funded by revenue from the oil and gas sector. Lula has also shown support for oil and gas as part of the energy mix. In recent weeks, he vowed to protect Brazil’s oil and critical mineral resources from foreign control.

Strong national policies and high levels of foreign investment have helped the South American country diversify its energy mix and solidify its position as a regional energy hub in recent years. With its strong track record, Brazil is expected to continue expanding its renewable energy as well as its fossil fuel capacity regardless of who wins the October presidential election.

By Felicity Bradstock for Oilprice.com

为何创纪录的高温未能推高美国天然气价格
电网级电池正在快速发展……
意昂神州（Enel）为冬奥会提供动力……
虽然分布式能源并不是……
费利西蒂·布拉德斯托克（Felicity Bradstock）是一位常驻墨西哥城的作家兼记者。她为能源网站撰稿，报道多个其他行业，并且还撰写……
得益于有利的本国政策以及外国投资者的支持，巴西正持续扩大其可再生能源装机容量。近年来，这个南美大国发展了令人瞩目的绿色能源产业，同时扩大了石油和天然气产量，以加强能源安全并树立其作为区域能源枢纽的声誉。
到2025年，巴西拥有令人赞叹的低碳能源结构，其约50%的能源来自太阳能、风能和生物能源等可再生能源。巴西通过实施主要侧重于能源安全的长期能源政策实现了这种多样化。2023年，巴西与能源相关的碳排放占该国温室气体总排放量的比例不足20%，而全球平均水平约为75%。
据巴西电力行业监管机构 Aneel 称，8月份巴西电网新增了约1.68吉瓦（GW）的太阳能、风能和火电装机容量。8月份共有20座新设施接入电网，其中包括15座太阳能电站、3座火力发电厂和2座风电场。这使得2026年迄今新增装机总量达到4.85吉瓦，其中太阳能占新增容量的3.5吉瓦。巴西目前的总发电装机容量达到221吉瓦，其中近85%来自可再生能源。
今年5月，世界银行执行董事会批准了一个新项目，以鼓励对巴西东北部工业和能源价值链中的低碳工业大宗商品、清洁燃料及配套基础设施进行投资。世界银行宣布提供5亿美元贷款，作为总额达9.68亿美元的一揽子更广泛融资计划的一部分，以协助巴西开发该地区基本尚未开发的丰富可再生能源资源。巴西东北部是该国最贫困的地区之一，发展清洁能源产业预计将创造就业机会并促进当地经济增长。
新开发银行（New Development Bank）也为东北部帕拉伊巴州的一处大型风电项目提供了融资。2025年10月，中国三峡集团的巴西子公司三峡巴西（CTG Brasil）建成了装机容量达648兆瓦（MW）的 Serra da Palmeira 风电综合体。
近年来，中巴两国深化了在可再生能源和清洁技术开发领域的合作，中国企业将尖端技术带到巴西以支持其可持续发展。两国的战略重点包括绿色发展、能源转型和再工业化。中国国家电网公司近期动工开建了一条全长1,468公里的特高压输电项目，这也是巴西历史上投资规模最大的输电特许经营权项目。
在即将于10月举行的总统选举前夕，商界团体正敦促各候选人支持绿色增长。代表11家巴西最大商业集团的巴西可持续发展商业委员会（CEBDS）在《2026年致总统候选人公开信》中向各候选人呼吁，应更加注重聚焦点、战略和治理，以增强巴西的竞争力和可持续发展能力。
在 CEBDS 可持续大会期间，该团体讨论了地缘政治与气候、不确定性下的投资、水资源可用性、发电以及粮食生产等议题。峰会还重点探讨了如何将巴西的可持续发展议程转化为经济优势。
CEBDS 主席兼2025年第三十届联合国气候变化大会（COP30）商界特使玛丽娜·格罗西（Marina Grossi）解释称：“在这封信中，我们试图为国家提出一个蓝图规划。这是一件能帮助我们向前迈进的事业，而不是让我们沦为仅仅出售初级大宗商品，同时还要提供气候解决方案。”
这封公开信强调了巴西的资产，包括清洁能源、肥沃的土壤、全球最大的生物多样性储备以及在生物燃料领域数十年的领先地位。CEBDS 在信中表示：“这种自然环境是我们最宝贵的经济基础设施，全世界都愿意为此买单。但没有任何竞争优势能够凭空持续：它需要规划、跨越历届政府的延续性政策，以及一个愿意将自然财富转化为长久繁荣的生产性行业。”
大选中的两位领先候选人分别是左翼总统路易斯·伊纳西奥·卢拉·达席尔瓦（Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva）和右翼参议员弗拉维奥·博索纳罗（Flávio Bolsonaro）。博索纳罗极力赞成油气扩张，并呼吁增加能源补贴。然而，尽管他持有气候否认论观点，但博索纳罗也承认绿色能源具有广泛的民意支持，并未将其排除在议程之外。
去年12月，在巴西于11月主办完 COP30 气候大会后，卢拉指示各部门在60天内为国家能源政策委员会（CNPE）起草一份关于能源转型的决议。其目标是减少巴西对石油、煤炭和天然气的依赖，并规划融资机制，包括设立由油气行业收入提供资金的能源转型基金（Energy Transition Fund）。卢拉同时也对将油气作为能源结构的一部分表示了支持。近几周来，他誓言保护巴西的石油和关键矿产资源不受外国控制。
强有力的国家政策和高水平的外国投资近年来帮助这个南美国家实现了能源结构多元化，并巩固了其作为区域能源枢纽的地位。凭借其良好的历史业绩，无论谁在10月的总统选举中获胜，预计巴西都将继续扩大其可再生能源以及化石燃料的产能。

Hi, friends! Welcome to Installer No. 145, your guide to the best and Verge-iest stuff in the world. (If you’re new here, welcome, I’m happy to be done traveling for a bit, and also you can read all the old editions at the Installer homepage.)

This week, I flew to San Francisco to try out Meta’s new hardware, including the impressive Meta VR Glasses. Along the way, I’ve been listening to Joanna Stern’s interview with Mark Zuckerberg, watching this interview with new Apple CEO John Ternus, revisiting Steve Jobs’ “Antennagate” press conference Q&A, playing games on my Steam Deck using the Xreal One Pro glasses, and reading Sarah Wynn-Williams’ Careless People when I have spare moments.

I also have for you more on Meta’s glasses, Remedy’s Control sequel, Microsoft’s updated Surface Mouse, and more.

Today I’m featuring The Verge’s Brad Bourque. Brad joined our commerce team for a few months to help out with our deals coverage and has been going deep into gaming tech. He’s also a fellow Portlander, so I had to feature him as one of our small but mighty Portland contingent.

I asked Brad to share his homescreen and the apps and things he cares about. Here it is, plus some info on the apps he uses and why:

The phone: Pixel 9 Pro XL

The wallpaper: My homescreen wallpaper is just an included Pixel wallpaper of plants in mellow green tones. My lockscreen is a fan-made Tekken Tag Tournament poster featuring Armor King and Modelo. It doesn’t have to make sense if the vibes are right.

I also asked Brad to share a few things he’s into right now. Here’s what he sent back:

Here’s what the Installer community is into this week. I want to know what you’re into right now as well! Email installer@theverge.com with your recommendations for anything and everything, and we’ll feature some of our favorites here every week. For even more great recommendations, check out the replies to this post on The Verge.

“I’ve been really enjoying a new app for my self-hosted media server. NostalgiaTV uses your media library to set up TV channels akin to classic cable. You turn it on and it brings up the ‘live’ TV guide/schedule and you can channel surf to choose what to watch instead of scrolling through your media library. Totally unnecessary and also way more fun than I thought it would be. They automatically set up a few channels for you, but you can also get in the weeds setting up custom channels and schedules.” — vikrael

“As a fan of the Planet Money podcast, I was surprised to come across their new book at my local library. Now being a few chapters into it, I am pleasantly surprised about how good of a read it is (especially if you enjoy the podcast). Title is Planet Money: A Guide to the Economic Forces That Shape Your Life.” — YG_400

“Currently reading The God of the Woods by Liz Moore that is being adapted into a Netflix show soon. The book is so good and hard to put down as the mystery draws you in as you hope for answers with each turn of the page.” — Sabertooth

“In the final act of Star Wars Zero Company. It is VERY good.” — BV

“I just recently got back into photography after years of just shooting on my iPhone and trying to tweak the results. Wow have I missed my Ricoh GRIII and Olympus XA2. While the Ricoh gives me instant gratification of capturing a moment exactly how I envisioned it, it’s been a lot of fun shooting rolls of film (stored in the freezer of course), and having to patiently wait for the results to come back!” — Ricky

Well, after my big tip in this section last week about eating at familiar restaurants while traveling, I wasn’t able to do any of that while traveling for Meta, and I felt it. Boy was I tired and hungry. It came down to a few different things, like a busier schedule and mostly being on Meta’s campus, where eating options were limited. I did get to devour some protein bars, which are a guilty pleasure of mine. But I really was hankering for some Chipotle.

topStories.title: 智能家居墓地正变得愈发拥挤
topStories.originalTitle: The smart home graveyard is getting crowded
topStories.snippet: This is The Stepback, a weekly newsletter breaking down one essential story from the tech world. For more on the fragile state of your connected devices, follow Jennifer Pattison Tuohy. The Stepback arrives in our subscribers' inboxes on Sunday at 8AM ET. Opt in for The Stepback here. With a built-in scale, restaurant-grade heating elements, a camera, and the intelligence to recognize a chicken breast an
topStories.fullContent:
Posts from this topic will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

The shutdown of June Oven is just another reminder that the cloud was never ours to keep.

Posts from this author will be added to your daily email digest and your homepage feed.

See All by Jennifer Pattison Tuohy

A decade ago, a group of former Apple engineers built a beautiful smart oven. With a built-in scale, restaurant-grade heating elements, a camera, and the intelligence to recognize a chicken breast and cook it perfectly, the June Oven set the standard for smart cooking appliances. At $1,495, it was absurdly expensive, but it quickly grew a small, devoted following that expanded when the company introduced a more modestly priced model.

This past Tuesday, June went dark. Weber, which bought the company in January 2021 and stopped making the ovens in 2022, shut off the app and cloud services, leaving its users with a sleek-looking toaster oven. There will be no app control, no software updates, and no new AI food recognition to crisp that strudel perfectly. You can still use it as an oven, but there will be no support or parts, and if you have to factory reset it for some reason, that could be the nail in the coffin. Weber told me it considered open-sourcing the technology for someone else to keep it alive, but decided against it, citing the fact June’s IP is part of its Weber Connect platform.

June is just the latest in a depressingly long list of connected products that have arrived in the smart home graveyard in the last two years alone. The Nest Secure, early Nest Thermostats, Belkin’s WeMo line, Neato’s robot vacuums, the Brava smart oven, Logitech’s Pop buttons, Bose’s SoundTouch speakers, and Sengled’s smart bulbs all lost their lifelines. While some were saved by local APIs and protocols — such as Zigbee, Thread, and Apple’s HomeKit, or a Home Assistant integration — most are like the June Oven, destined to live out their days in a zombie state.

The silver lining, if you want to see it, is that most of these gadgets degrade rather than die outright. June and Brava will still work as ovens. Nest Thermostats can still control your heating and cooling, just like the $30 plastic wall wart they replaced, and a Neato will still vacuum your floors. But the remote access, voice control, updates, and other smart features you bought the devices for are gone. Some — like Nest Secure — are now pure e-waste.

There’s always the possibility of a rescue, but it’s rare. Some enterprising user may figure out a way to connect a headless corpse to Home Assistant, the open-source platform that has become the default refuge for the smart home undead. When smart lighting platform Insteon shut down in 2022, its users bought the company and resurrected it. Bose reversed course and open-sourced its SoundTouch API, and Pebble’s founder brought the iconic smartwatch back to life after the Rebble alliance kept it on life support. June’s co-founder Matt Van Horn said on X that he tried to keep the servers online but to no avail.

The smart home has reached a tipping point. Many of its early pioneers are aging out — a decade plus is a long time for a startup. Most have been bought by bigger companies, likely attracted by the shiny thing but then quickly dismayed by the bottom line. Back then, a cloud server was cheaper to build than a local hub, but servers continue to cost money, and once a company decides to shut down a product, reasons to keep paying fade rapidly. This appears to be what’s happening to Level Lock, another former-Apple-engineer startup that produced a beautiful replacement for a common household item. Assa Abloy bought the smart lock company and abruptly fired most of the team. It’s still alive, but how long it will continue is a big question.

Three things need to happen to prevent the smart home from burning more users: we need consumer protections; manufacturers need to step up and build in safeguards; we need to know how to protect ourselves.

Consumer Reports is pushing for legislation around connected IoT devices, including making manufacturers push a local API to a device before killing its cloud. This would allow it to keep talking to a platform like Home Assistant instead of becoming a paperweight. This is essentially what Bose did with SoundTouch, and other companies should follow that lead (I’m not holding my breath on legislation).

When building a connected device, manufacturers need to make it function without the cloud. Include physical buttons so it doesn’t rely on an app, and use local protocols alongside any cloud connectivity. This is a key issue the smart home standard Matter was designed to address: Matter devices can retain many functions in a Matter platform, regardless of what happens to the manufacturer’s business. Other local protocols like Zigbee, Z-Wave, Thread, and Bluetooth similarly help futureproof products.

I fully agree with Stacey Higginbotham’s advice to manufacturers that they need to “design for death from day one,” or at the very least plan to pay for the funeral. Amazon refunded anyone who bought a Halo in the 12 months before it killed the fitness band. Vorwerk promised to keep Neato running for five years; when that was truncated to two, it at least gave some users free replacements. Google offered Nest Secure customers a free replacement from ADT. None of this beats a device that doesn’t need the cloud to function, but it helps ease the pain.

My advice if you’re buying a smart home device remains the same. Make sure it offers local control, has physical buttons (or a direct remote control), and can operate “offline.” Don’t dismiss cloud-connected features; they can add real value, but remember that any feature reliant on a server could one day die. A gadget that only talks to the cloud is already halfway in the grave.

June智能烤箱的停运再次提醒我们：云端服务从来就不真正属于我们。
来自该作者的帖子将被添加到您的每日电子邮件文摘和主页动态中。
查看詹妮弗·帕蒂森·图伊（Jennifer Pattison Tuohy）的全部文章
十年前，一群前苹果工程师打造了一款外观精美的智能烤箱。凭借内置称重秤、餐厅级发热元件、摄像头，以及能自动识别鸡胸肉并完美烤熟的智能技术，June Oven树立了智能烹饪电器的标杆。当时1495美元的售价堪称昂贵得离谱，但它迅速吸引了一小群忠实拥趸；随着该公司随后推出价格更亲民的型号，用户群体进一步扩大。
就在刚刚过去的周二，June陷入了沉寂。于2021年1月收购该公司的Weber在2022年停止生产该系列烤箱，如今更是直接切断了应用程序和云端服务，留给用户的只剩下一台外观时尚的普通烤箱。未来将不再有应用控制、不再有软件更新，也不会再有新的AI食物识别来把馅饼烤得恰到好处。你仍然可以把它当成普通烤箱使用，但不会再有任何售后支持或零部件供应；如果出于某种原因你必须将其恢复出厂设置，那可能就会成为压垮它的最后一颗钉子。Weber告诉我，他们曾考虑过将该技术开源以便其他人能维持其运转，但最终决定放弃，理由是June的知识产权属于其Weber Connect平台的一部分。
仅在过去两年里，流入智能家居墓地的联网产品名单就长得令人沮丧，而June只是其中的最新一例。Nest Secure安防系统、早期Nest恒温器、贝尔金的WeMo产品线、Neato扫地机器人、Brava智能烤箱、罗技Pop按钮、Bose SoundTouch音箱以及生迪（Sengled）智能灯泡，全部失去了生存命脉。虽然有部分产品通过本地API和协议——如Zigbee、Thread、苹果HomeKit或Home Assistant集成——得以幸免于难，但大多数产品都和June Oven一样，注定要在僵尸状态中度过余生。
如果非要说有什么一线生机的话，那就是这些设备大多数只是功能降级，而非彻底报废。June和Brava依然能充当烤箱使用；Nest恒温器仍然能控制家里的冷暖气，就像它们当初替代的那个价值30美元的塑料墙插温控器一样；Neato也依然能帮你清扫地板。但是，当初促使你购买这些设备所看重的远程访问、语音控制、固件更新以及其他智能功能，都已不复存在。而其中一些设备——比如Nest Secure——现在则彻底沦为了电子垃圾。
拯救的希望并非完全没有，但实属罕见。某些善于折腾的用户可能会想出办法，将失去“大脑”的硬件躯壳接入Home Assistant——这个开源平台已经成为智能家居“活死人”的默认避难所。2022年智能照明平台Insteon停运时，其用户群干脆买下了这家公司并使其起死回生。Bose随后改变了策略，开源了其SoundTouch API；而在Rebble联盟为其维持生命后，Pebble的创始人让这款标志性智能手表重获新生。June的联合创始人马特·范霍恩（Matt Van Horn）在X平台上表示，他曾努力维持服务器在线，但最终无济于事。
智能家居已经走到了一个临界点。许多早期的行业先驱正步入暮年——对初创公司而言，十年以上已经是漫长的岁月。其中大多数被大公司收购，买家起初往往被亮眼的新技术所吸引，但很快就对财务底线感到失望。在当年，搭建云服务器比研发本地中枢成本更低，但服务器需要持续烧钱；一旦公司决定停掉一款产品，继续为其付费的理由便迅速化为乌有。这似乎也是Level Lock正在遭遇的命运——这家同样由前苹果工程师创办的初创公司，曾为常见家居用品打造了极其精美的替代方案。亚萨合莱（Assa Abloy）收购了这家智能门锁公司，随后突然解雇了大部分团队成员。它目前仍在勉强运转，但还能撑多久是一个巨大的问号。
为了防止智能家居继续伤害更多用户，必须做好三件事：我们需要完善的消费者权益保护；制造商需要行动起来建立保障机制；我们自己也需要懂得如何自保。
《消费者报告》（Consumer Reports）正在推动针对物联网联网设备的立法，包括强制制造商在关闭云端服务之前，必须向设备推送本地API。这样一来，设备便能继续与Home Assistant等平台通信，而不至于沦为一块摆设。这基本上就是Bose对待SoundTouch的做法，其他公司也应当效仿（但我对立法落地并不抱太大希望）。
在研发联网设备时，制造商需要让其在脱离云端的情况下依然能够运转。提供物理按键以摆脱对应用的依赖，并在提供云端连接的同时兼容本地协议。这正是智能家居标准Matter旨在解决的核心痛点：无论制造商的商业运营发生何种变故，Matter设备都能在Matter平台上保留诸多功能。类似地，Zigbee、Z-Wave、Thread和蓝牙等其他本地协议，也有助于让产品具备面向未来的持久生命力。
我完全赞同斯泰西·希金博瑟姆（Stacey Higginbotham）给制造商提出的建议：他们必须“从第一天起就为消亡做好设计”，或者退一步说，至少要做好支付丧葬费用的准备。亚马逊在关停Halo健康手环前，为过去12个月内购买该设备的所有用户办理了退款。福维克（Vorwerk）曾承诺让Neato继续运转五年；当这一期限缩短至两年时，它至少为部分用户提供了免费替换产品。谷歌则为Nest Secure客户提供了来自ADT的免费替代设备。这些举措虽比不上那些完全无需云端即可运转的设备，但至少能减轻用户的损失与痛苦。
如果你打算购买智能家居设备，我的建议依然如故：务必确保它支持本地控制，配有物理按键（或直连遥控器），并且能够在“离线”状态下运作。不要完全排斥云端互联功能，它们确实能带来实用价值，但请时刻记住：任何依赖服务器的功能，终有一天都可能会随之消亡。一款只能同云端通信的设备，半只脚其实已经踏进了坟墓。

topStories.originalTitle: OpenAI Feared "Optics" of what might appear on Hacker News
topStories.fullContent:
Added to last week’s revelations, new filings reveal OpenAI's lawless determination to do virtually anything to win the AI arms race, including using books from a “sketchy Russian website” and releasing products “that will make people unemployed”

(New York, September 21, 2026) Explosive new documents released last Thursday in Authors Guild v. OpenAI—the major book authors’ ongoing lawsuit alleging OpenAI and Microsoft illegally trained their products on copyrighted books—show that executives and employees at both companies intentionally broke the law and their disdain for human authorship. The brief meticulously documents AI developers’ knowledge of the damage their actions could do to authors, publishers, and American culture itself, warning that “OpenAI’s GPT models pose an existential threat to those who write and publish books.”

Plaintiffs in the lawsuit include The Authors Guild, writers David Baldacci, Taylor Branch, Michael Connelly, Sylvia Day, Jonathan Franzen, Christopher Golden, Andrew Sean Greer, John Grisham, David Henry Hwang, Matthew Klam, George R.R. Martin, Jodi Picoult, Stacy Schiff, James Shapiro, and others. Their filings (here and here) mark a turning point in the case, putting the defendant companies’ guilty knowledge and reckless actions at the center of the narrative.

Authors Guild CEO Mary Rasenberger observed, “These filings reveal shocking disdain for writers and their work through repeated, intentional decisions to steal books rather than pay for them with full knowledge that their products will destroy the careers of authors. OpenAI pursued its mass piracy scheme even in the face of clear evidence that doing so would degrade American culture by substituting human works with AI slop and would put thousands of writers out of work. We are grateful to our entire legal team for uncovering and telling this critical story.”

Alongside equally scorching but separate revelations in a brief filed by news media organizations, the authors’ brief reveals:

All quotes taken from Class Plaintiffs’ Memorandum of Law in Support of Motion for Partial Summary Judgment (Docket 1982) and Class Plaintiffs’ Corrected Rule 56.1 Statement of Undisputed Material Facts (Docket 1987).

This briefing was filed in the class action case brought on behalf of the Authors Guild and book copyright owners, Alter v. OpenAI and Microsoft, with lead counsel Justin A. Nelson from Susman Godfrey. The case is part of multidistrict litigation against those defendants pending in Manhattan. We expect more briefing over the next couple months and a hearing in early 2027.

With more than 18,000 members, the Authors Guild is the nation’s oldest and largest professional organization for published writers. It advocates on behalf of working writers to protect free speech, freedom of expression, and authors’ copyrights; fights for fair contracts and authors ability to earn a livable wage; and provides a welcoming community for writers and translators of fiction, nonfiction, poetry, and journalism. Through its educational and charitable arm, the Authors Guild Foundation, it also offers free programming to teach working writers about the business of writing, as well as organizing public events that highlight the importance of a rich, diverse American literary culture and the authors who contribute to it.

topStories.title: 互联网发现了 TLA+。接下来呢？
topStories.originalTitle: The internet discovers TLA+. Now what?
topStories.fullContent:
By Anna Mészáros, Szilvia Ujváry, Kseniia Strelbytska, Balázs Szilágyi, and Ferenc Huszár

Boris Cherny’s viral TLA+ tweet showed how useful formal models can be in agentic coding. This post gives a practical introduction to what TLA+ is.But TLA+ is only the starting point. We also look at how temporal specifications, modern proof systems and AI agents can fit together, from modeling system behaviour to generating machine-checked proofs, and ultimately toward software that is specified, implemented and verified in one loop. We also give a sneak peek into some of our work at Reasonable on making this possible.

This week Boris Cherny graced TLA+, a formal modeling toolkit that is over 30 years old, with a tweet. He used Opus 5.5 to model parts of the Claude Agent SDK in TLA+ and Lean, and the internet did what it does: ~1M views, thousands of bookmarks, and people are asking what TLA+ actually is. Boris's post is a great showcase, and it adds to early examples showing that TLA+ is well worth the effort in agentic coding: see Datadog's post on harness-first agents.If you are one of the people now wondering what TLA+ is and what it is for, you are in the right place. TLA+ happens to be one of the formal techniques our team has dived deep into.But there is also a larger reason we care about it. TLA+ gives us a compact language for saying what a system is allowed to do and what must always or eventually be true of it. That is a useful starting point for verification, but it is not the end of the story.Here is the short version:

TLA+ describes possible system behaviours and the properties those behaviours should satisfy.

TLA+ itself does not fully verify an implementation. It checks a model of the software, not the software itself, and its main model checker only explores finite instances.

Modern proof systems can take us further. In Verus, specification, proof and Rust implementation can live in the same language.

AI can already automate part of this process. We built an agentic pipeline that turned 16,000+ TLA+ specification/property pairs into 3,000+ machine-checked Verus proofs.

Part of our work at Reasonable is training models to enable agents to do this, consistently, reliably, quickly.

Our running example is the one in the interactive playground below, where three computers, a, b and c, have to agree on which of them is the leader. Databases rely on leader election being correct. We require that no two leaders exist at the same time. You can click through the playground to learn the basics of TLA+ through the five levels of the game.

TLA+ (Temporal Logic of Actions) is a language for writing down two kinds of objects:

A transition system: what the system can do. There are states, which are snapshots of the system (who is a candidate, who has voted for whom, who is leader) and actions, single steps that change a state ("a starts an election", "b votes for a"). In the interactive playground, you take these steps by hand, exploring one possible run the way a tester would.

Temporal properties are statements about how a run plays out over time. For example, "There are never two leaders." "A leader is eventually elected."

A TLA+ model declares legal system states and allowed transitions between these states. For example, in the election, any of a, b or c may start an election from the initial state, voting for itself as it does so, and b may vote for a or for c.It imposes no order on transitions and does not attempt to model the probability distribution of different events happening, which is the right abstraction for distributed systems, where messages, timeouts and user actions can happen in many different orders.The underlying mathematics is simple, it uses sets, true/false statements and relations. Temporal properties are then built from operators over executions:

□ P (always P ): P holds in every state visited.

◇ P (eventually P ): P holds in some future state.

P ⇝ Q (P leads to Q): whenever P holds, Q eventually holds afterwards.

Two kinds of property matter particularly often.Safety: nothing bad ever happens. For our election: □ (there are never two leaders). In the playground, the model checker explores every possible state: all 38 states for three computers, and confirms the property. Level 2 changes one rule so that a computer can vote twice. The checker then returns a six-step execution ending with two leaders. That execution is a counterexample: a concrete way the model can violate the property.Liveness: something good eventually happens. Safety alone is not enough. A system that does nothing forever is perfectly safe. So we might also require: ◇ (someone is leader). Level 3 shows why this matters: a typo stops anything from happening, and the safety check still passes. Liveness requires fairness assumptions, which rule out executions where an action remains possible forever but is simply never taken. Weak fairness WF(A) says that an action that stays enabled must eventually happen; strong fairness SF(A) covers actions that become enabled infinitely often.The mental model is simple: a TLA+ model describes the possible execution traces of a system, and a property describes which traces are acceptable. Verification asks whether every possible trace is acceptable.TLC, the standard TLA+ model checker, answers this by enumerating reachable states for a finite instance. A proof makes the stronger statement that the property holds in general.For more, Jack Vanlightly has been teaching TLA+ on his blog long before agents made it fashionable

TLA+ is increasingly widely deployed because this way of reasoning about systems can be practically useful; you'll see it in use at AWS, MongoDB, and Datadog, in Kafka, and many other places. But there are three important caveats, where TLA+ alone stops short of full software verification.Model checking only goes so far. In practice, people most often use TLA+ with TLC. TLC explores every possible run, but only for a finite model. In our example, the state space grows from 38 states with three computers to more than a million with nine. To establish a property for arbitrary system sizes, you need a proof. TLA+'s own prover, TLAPS, can do this in some cases, but its automation is limited, particularly for liveness arguments.The model is not the implementation. A TLA+ specification is usually a separate model of the software. Nothing automatically guarantees that the implementation behaves exactly like the model, and the two can drift apart as the code changes. This is one element of the classic spec-to-implementation gap.TLA+ cannot express every property we may want. TLA+ is based on linear temporal logic, which makes statements about individual executions: "In every run, a leader is eventually elected." But some interesting properties concern alternative futures or strategies.

CTL, a branching-time logic, can express statements such as: "from any state, a new election can still be started."

ATL can express strategic statements such as: "this computer has a strategy to become a leader whatever the others do."

These richer properties become relevant once we start thinking about systems containing multiple competing or collaborating agents.So TLA+ gives us an unusually useful language for describing temporal behaviour, but a complete verification stack needs more: stronger proof machinery, a connection to real code, and eventually richer logics.

One route is to take the model into a modern proof system. There are several options, examples include:

Lean is interactive: you (or an AI) write the proof step by step. It is very general, widely used in mathematics, and was the prover used in Boris's post.

Verus is auto-active and designed around Rust. You provide specifications and the important proof structure, while an automated solver handles much of the lower-level reasoning.

Veil is a Lean-based tool built specifically for state-machine models. Leo de Moura has recommended it, and it was recently used to verify a sync engine, fixing 17 bugs in the process. Liveness remains future work, however, and the verified model is still separate from the implementation.

Why use Verus? Because specifications and proofs can live alongside the real Rust implementation. That matters because it gives us a route towards closing the spec-to-implementation gap: instead of proving properties only about a separate abstract model, we can ultimately prove that the implementation refines that model. Systems such as Anvil have already demonstrated this style of verification; our work at Reasonable builds particularly closely on Anvil.Why automate formal verification? The proofs involved are often less exotic than the phrase formal verification suggests.

Safety proofs are usually inductive. Show that the property holds initially, then show that every possible action preserves it. Much of the work consists of splitting over the different actions and tracking the relevant invariants.

Liveness proofs establish progress. Typically, some quantity decreases as the system progresses, together with fairness assumptions ruling out executions in which an enabled action is postponed forever. Rules such as WF1, WF2, SF1 and SF2 package these arguments; our temporal library implements them as proven Verus lemmas.

A large fraction of this work is repetitive: tracking invariants, splitting over actions, supplying intermediate lemmas and filling in solver-visible details. That makes it a natural target for proof-generating agents.

Automated theorem proving has recently made rapid progress in mathematics. Software verification poses a somewhat different problem: before proving anything, we need a useful description of what the software is supposed to do.TLA+ is attractive here because temporal specifications are relatively compact and readable, and because many real systems already have TLA+ models. If we can connect those models to modern proof systems and to implementations, several directions become possible.

Refinement proofs. Prove that the Rust implementation follows the TLA+ model. Anvil demonstrated this manually. Automating more of that process would reduce the gap between verifying a model and verifying the software that implements it.

Program synthesis. Start from the model and generate an implementation together with a proof that the implementation refines it. In this setting, the formal specification constrains both code generation and verification.

Protocol search. Once checking a candidate protocol is cheap enough, the verifier can become an objective function: generate variants of a protocol, verify them, and retain those satisfying the desired properties. This starts to look similar to systems such as AlphaEvolve, except that correctness is checked formally rather than estimated by tests.

Beyond linear time. Some properties of multi-agent systems concern alternative futures or strategies rather than individual execution traces. Expressing those requires logics beyond LTL. Benjamin Brast-McKie's work explores this side of the problem, while our current work focuses on proving temporal properties and connecting them to programs.

We have been working on a pipeline for translating TLA+ specifications into machine-checked Verus proofs. Our next blog posts will describe the individual pieces in more detail. For now, the main results are:

A TLA+ to Verus transpiler. We built an algorithmic transpiler and compared it with an agentic alternative in which an LLM produces the translation and a second LLM reviews it.

A prover–reviewer loop with anti-cheat checks. One agent writes a proof and another reviews it. A separate gatekeeper checks that the agents have not modified the specification or introduced shortcuts such as assume(false).

A dataset of temporal proofs in Verus. Starting from 16,459 real-world TLA+ specification/property pairs, the pipeline produced more than 3,000 machine-checked safety and liveness proofs. We also constructed a 40-task evaluation set.

An evaluation of current models. We tested both closed and open-weight frontier models on the evaluation set, looking at which temporal proofs they can complete and where the remaining failure modes are.

We'll cover those results in the follow-up posts.

We're hiring people excited to push the boundaries of formal verification and AI agents. If you want to help build systems where correctness can be machine-checked, we'd love to hear from you: Careers.We're also eager to hear from teams building systems where correctness really matters. We're exploring what machine-checked proofs can unlock for real-world applications and we'd love to talk: Contact.
